runs.text: Ten Jewish surnames. Ten towns on a map. Shapiro comes from Speyer, in Germany. In the Middle Ages, it was called Spira. Oppenheimer: Oppenheim. Mintz: Mainz. Landau: Landau. Halpern: Heilbronn. Ginzburg: Gunzburg. Horowitz: Horovice, in today's Czech Republic. Prager: Prague. Wiener: Vienna. Posner: Poznan, Poland. Why towns? In seventeen eighty seven, Austria's emperor ordered every Jew to take a surname. Many simply took the name of the town they came from. But some names hide something much older. Katz: Hebrew initials for righteous priest. Segal: Hebrew initials for Levite deputy. Priests and Levites served in the Temple in Jerusalem. Not every Shapiro or Katz is Jewish, and family stories vary. Where does your surname come from? Tell me in the comments. If you like Israel facts, follow <<n|oʊ|ˈ|ɑ|m>> <<ˈ|r|ɑː|z>> for more. So, what's hiding in your name?
